tagline: Up the Columbia's north bank, from lush woods to desert hills.
intro: SR 14 leaves Washougal on the north bank of the Columbia, past the wildlife refuges at Steigerwald Lake, Franz Lake and Pierce, and on by Bonneville Dam and the Bridge of the Gods to Stevenson. East of there it goes through a series of tunnels along the river, crosses the White Salmon and then the Klickitat at Lyle, and leaves the national scenic area just short of Maryhill.

The country changes on the way, from lush forest in the west to rolling hills and desert country in the east. The first road through the gorge on this side was a wagon road surveyed in 1905 between Washougal and Lyle.
season: State of Washington Tourism notes wildflowers and more visitors in spring and summer, and calls fall the more peaceful time to go.

moments.title: Bridge of the Gods
moments.text: In September 1927 onlookers watched Charles Lindbergh fly the Spirit of St. Louis low over the new bridge, turn around and come back underneath it.

moments.title: Bingen
moments.text: P.J. Suksdorf named his town in 1892 for Bingen am Rhein, though here it is said BIN-jen, and it looks across the river to Mount Hood.

moments.title: Maryhill
moments.text: Sam Hill, born a Quaker, built a concrete Stonehenge here for Klickitat County's dead of the First World War, and when his town burned the replica was left standing.
